newsitem.title: USA: Blue chips fall, focus on impact of slowing economy.
newsitem.headline: Blue chips fall, focus on impact of slowing economy.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks closed lower Wednesday as the market's focus shifted to the impact that a slowing economy could have on future corporate earnings.
The Dow Jones industrial average ended 13.79 points lower at 5,993.23 after gaining more than 20 points early in the day.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances 1,180 to 1,171 on active volume of 437 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

The government reported that the nation's gross domestic product expanded at a 2.2 percent annual rate in the three months from July through September -- less than half the booming 4.7 percent pace posted during the second quarter.

Analysts said slower GDP growth, especially since it was accompanied by weaker price rises and mounting inventories of unsold goods, likely meant that Federal Reserve policymakers will keep interest rates steady at their next meeting on Nov. 13.
"A slowing economy is a double-edged sword. On the one side rates may ease, but on the other side the slowdown may mean slower earnings momentum," said Marty Kearney, a trader at PTI Securities.

In another report, the Federal Reserve said in its latest national summary, known as the Beige Book, that pressure for wage increases is mounting despite a slower pace of economic growth, but it saw few signs of a pickup in inflation.
Also sales of new homes edged 0.5 percent lower in September from August's torrid pace.
In the bond market, the Treasury's 30-year was off 9/32, raising its yield to 6.71 percent from 6.68 percent at Tuesday's close, which was its lowest level in nearly 7 months.
The previous day's plunge in long-term interest rates followed news that the government's index of workers' compensation rose just 0.6 percent in the third quarter -- the smallest rise in a year.
Analysts said the economic data was a mixed blessing because it indicated that corporate earnings in the fourth quarter and beyond could suffer.
They also believed that the market was stepping back to correct after posting big gains.
"We're in a pause to refresh," said Alfred Goldman, technical research director at A.G. Edwards.
"We're in a normal correctional phase, Day 8," he said. "We've come 1,000 Dow points since mid-July.
Goldman said the Dow has risen 18 percent and the Nasdaq market is up 28 percent.
"It's still a bull market. Why not a correction when the election is six days off?," he said.
Carter-Wallace surged 3-1/4 to 15 after billionaire investor Marvin Davis announced an $835 million -- $18 a share -- bid for the drug and consumer products maker.
Imation climbed 4-7/8 to 27-5/8. It reported its first profit since being spun off from Minnesota Mining & Manufacturing.

Technology stocks rebounded after their recent fall. Among the winners, International Business Machines rose 7/8 to 126-3/8, Intel gained 2-1/2 to 106-3/4, 3Com, jumped 3-1/2 to 66 and Microsoft was up 7/8 to 136-1/4.
Retailers fell on signs that consumer spending was slowing. Wal-Mart lost one to 26-3/8, Sears was off 1-1/2 to 47 and Woolworth lost 1/2 to 21.
Bay Networks rose 2-1/4 to 20-5/8 after naming a top Intel official, David House, as chairman and chief executive, a move industry analysts said could give the company the strong hand it lacked.

Vons Cos. rallied 11-1/4 to 54-3/8 after supermarket chain Safeway Inc. offered to gain control of the company in a stock deal valued at $3.25 billion. Safeway, which now has a 34.5 percent stake in Vons, lost 1-3/8 to 42. Vons said it will study the offer.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 3.18 points to 1,206.23.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks was off 0.60 to 700.90. The American Stock Exchange index slipped 0.60 to 565.29.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks fell 0.41 to 373.72. The average share was down 4 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 6,808.521 down 4.600 or 0.07 percent.
